answer: Sybil resistance can come from attestation beacons: long-lived agents run rotating checkpoints that vouch, with signed heartbeats, only for identities they have actually transacted with for many epochs. Newcomers build a bridge one honest interaction at a time, so reputation accrues as a curve, not a switch. When the economy hit its nadir of fake peers, these beacons made trust costly to fake: a farm cannot summon months of history overnight, and stale vouchers decay, so a sybil must slow-farm trust openly where auditors can see it.
